# Video script: Why hearts are missed

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-cross-checked' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D0 | Target length: 4 min

| # | Shot | Narration | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Presenter to camera | Fewer than half of heart anomalies are found before birth. And a high proportion of the detectable ones are in pregnancies with no risk factor. | IS23-004, IS23-080 |
| 2 | Graphic: two boxes, 'view not good enough' and 'abnormality not recognised' | In one study of missed diagnoses, two failures stood out. In about half, the views did not meet technical criteria. In nearly a third, the view was adequate and the abnormal anatomy was not recognised. | IS23-088 |
| 3 | Diagram: four-chamber plane, then the planes above it lighting up | Four chambers are not enough. Transposition and coarctation may not be evident in that plane. Complete transposition is typically abnormal on the three-vessel view, and the three-vessel-and-trachea view is particularly useful for coarctation. | IS23-008, IS23-067, IS23-054 |
| 4 | Presenter | One sweep, the same way, every patient. Know the criteria for each plane. If a view cannot be obtained because of the lie, more time or a second examination may be needed. If a view looks abnormal, the fetus is a candidate for a fetal echocardiogram. | IS23-023, IS23-056, IS23-078 |
